statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-32281 (GO-2026-4946): in the Go standard library's crypto/x509 package, validating an otherwise trusted certificate chain whose certificates carry a very large number of policy mappings is unexpectedly slow, a possible denial of service. It is fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4946, https://go.dev/issue/78281, https://go.dev/cl/758061, the release-branch.go1.26 backport https://github.com/golang/go/commit/8028a514303f7cbc818094c05df33d1bbb3adb5a (in go1.26.2, not go1.26.1), https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU . We read every published alertmanager-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to 0.35.0-r2, x86_64 and aarch64, each download checked against the repository index checksum. Each package holds two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the Go Cryptographic Module (GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c) and linked with -s -w, so we read their function tables from the Go line table, which works on these stripped binaries, and found runtime.main in every one. The Go toolchain recorded in the build information, the same for both programs and both architectures, is: 0.31.1-r0 with Go 1.25.7; 0.31.1-r1 to 0.31.1-r4 with Go 1.26.1; 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r0 with Go 1.26.2; 0.32.1-r1 to 0.32.1-r2 with Go 1.26.3; 0.32.1-r3 to 0.33.1-r0 with Go 1.26.4; 0.33.1-r1 to 0.33.1-r3 with Go 1.26.5; 0.33.1-r5 to 0.34.0-r0 with Go 1.26.6; 0.34.0-r1 with Go 1.26.7; 0.34.0-r2 to 0.34.1-r1 with Go 1.26.8; 0.34.1-r2 to 0.34.1-r3 with Go 1.26.9; 0.34.1-r4 to 0.35.0-r0 with Go 1.26.10; 0.35.0-r1 to 0.35.0-r2 with Go 1.26.11. The Go vulnerability database lists crypto/x509 Certificate.Verify and policiesValid; the function tables of both programs contain both in every build, so the status follows the Go release. The builds before 0.31.1-r5 (0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r4) use Go 1.25.7 or 1.26.1, inside the affected range; 0.31.1-r5 and every later build use Go 1.26.2 to 1.26.11, which carry the fix, so 0.31.1-r5 is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-32281 (GO-2026-4946): crypto/x509 in the Go standard library validated certificate chains that use policies inefficiently when certificates contain a very large number of policy mappings, which can cause a denial of service. Only otherwise trusted chains, issued by a root in VerifyOptions.Roots or the system pool, are affected. It is fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2, and Go 1.27 releases include the fix: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4946, https://go.dev/issue/78281, https://go.dev/cl/758061, the release-branch.go1.26 backport https://github.com/golang/go/commit/8028a514303f7cbc818094c05df33d1bbb3adb5a (in go1.26.2, not go1.26.1), https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU. We read every published external-dns-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published: 33 builds, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, x86_64 and aarch64, each download checked against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the Go Cryptographic Module (GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c) that has no ELF interpreter and no dynamic section. The Go toolchain recorded in each program's build information, the same on both architectures, is: 0.20.0-r0 with Go 1.25.7; 0.20.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r0 with Go 1.26.1; 0.21.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r2 with Go 1.26.2; 0.21.0-r3 to 0.21.0-r5 with Go 1.26.3; 0.21.0-r6 to 0.21.0-r7 with Go 1.26.4; 0.21.0-r8 to 0.21.0-r11 with Go 1.26.5; 0.21.0-r12 with Go 1.26.6; 0.21.0-r13 to 0.22.0-r0 with Go 1.26.7; 0.22.0-r1 to 0.22.0-r3 with Go 1.26.8; 0.23.0-r1 to 0.23.0-r2 with Go 1.27.1; 0.23.0-r3 with Go 1.27.2; 0.23.0-r4 to 0.24.0-r2 with Go 1.27.3; 0.24.0-r3 to 0.24.0-r5 with Go 1.27.4. The program in every build contains crypto/x509.(*Certificate).Verify and policiesValid, found by name in its Go function table with runtime.main as a control in the same scan, so the vulnerable code is linked and the Go version decides. Builds 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r0 were built with a Go release inside the affected range. The range ends at 0.21.0-r1, the first published build made with a fixed Go release.
